clue.text: Repair on outside of a church is put at risk

indicators.note: the repair word is placed around the outside of the next pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to repair something is to mend it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Building work on the exterior of a church has put the structure in jeopardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word; the definition is the past participle phrase that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To menace is to threaten, so something menaced has been put in danger.

clue.text: I'd come out to see doctor maybe

indicators.note: out signals the letters are taken apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient says they have come out to visit the physician.
explanation.definitionFit: Medico is an informal term for a medical practitioner or student, a physician for example.

clue.text: No archdeacon wants a form of worship lasting days

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: A senior cleric is refusing a lengthy religious service.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon in the Church of England carries the title 'the Venerable', shortened to Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: A Catholic devotion of prayers said over nine successive days is a multi-day form of worship.

clue.text: Everyone stuck in city (nearly all) — notice a yen to pack up

indicators.note: one word is stuck inside the other, enclosed by it
nearly all of the word is used, the last letter removed

parts.note: the plain word city
everyone means all
an ad is a notice or advertisement
Y is the abbreviation for the yen currency

explanation.surface: Stuck in a busy city, someone sees a sign and longs to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like a longing but is the Japanese currency; 'stuck in' places the everyone word within the trimmed city.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop working for the time being is an idiom meaning to pack up for the day.

clue.text: Trick with which Venice's magistrate entertains Duke

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of Venice

explanation.surface: A cunning ploy by which the Venetian ruler hosts a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a cunning ruse or wheeze, a synonym for a trick.

clue.text: In high spirits, having got full pay organised

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is cheerful because their wages have come through in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frisky and full of fun is a synonym for being in high spirits.

clue.text: Elect an MP to be manoeuvred into position

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves the letters around into a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Voters choose a parliamentarian who will be steered into a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Placement is the act of putting something in a particular location, a synonym for positioning.

clue.text: Teach yourself? Involves feeling some pain

indicators.note: the letters are contained within the phrase teach yourself

explanation.surface: Self-teaching proves a painful business.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sore or aching is to feel some discomfort, a mild pain.

clue.text: Canterbury pilgrim with tale is outspoken, having left home

parts.note: an outspoken person is frank
in means at home

explanation.surface: A storytelling traveller speaks candidly after leaving his house.
explanation.walkthrough: In Chaucer's Canterbury Tales each pilgrim tells a story; one is a wealthy landowner whose tale is included.
explanation.definitionFit: In Chaucer's Canterbury Tales this landowning character is one of the pilgrims and tells a tale.

clue.text: Similarly funny in the manner of one in double act?

parts.note: like means in the manner of
Ernie Wise was half of the comedy double act Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: Asks if a comedian copies the style of a comic partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' qualifies the double act: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British TV comedy duo.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in the same way or also, a synonym for similarly.

clue.text: Troublemaker existed for revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns the word round, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: to have existed is to have lived

explanation.surface: An agitator was around to stir up a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' looks political but signals reading the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child or rogue is often called a little devil, a synonym for a troublemaker.

clue.text: Cast showing absence of life

parts.note: a plaster or wax cast taken of a face after the person has died

explanation.surface: A troupe of actors so lifeless they might as well be dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests a group of actors giving a dull show; it is a moulded impression of a corpse's face.
explanation.definitionFit: A moulded likeness of a dead person's features is the cast of a face that no longer lives.

clue.text: A tin recycled in cunning mechanical device

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the word for cunning

parts.note: cunning means clever

indicators.note: recycling turns the letters into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A tin can is reused to build an ingenious gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' shuffles A TIN, and 'in' places the result inside the cunning word, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A projecting beam supported at one end works as a lever, a mechanical device in engineering.

clue.text: Slanting southern gardens

parts.note: Kew Gardens are the Royal Botanic Gardens in London

explanation.surface: Describes sloping gardens in the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the famous botanic garden in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something askew or at an angle is oblique, so the word works as an adjective for slanting.

clue.text: Out of trouble, being unable to receive calls

definitions.meaning: freed from a difficulty or obligation
a telephone receiver left lifted from its cradle cannot ring

explanation.surface: Someone escapes blame by making themselves unreachable by phone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means let off from blame, and literally a lifted receiver gives an engaged line.

clue.text: Ablest two fit to engage in intellectual competition

indicators.note: the letters engage, grappling with one another until they form a new order

explanation.surface: The two cleverest people are ready to take part in a battle of brains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like a description of the two contestants but belongs to the letters being rearranged; 'to engage' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest of clever repartee or debate between sharp minds is an idiom for an intellectual competition.

clue.text: By contrast, the little knight may have an advantage

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
a gain is an advantage

explanation.surface: A minor knight may hold the upper hand, unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess notation N stands for knight, since K is the king.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces an opposing thought, an idiom meaning on the other hand.

clue.text: Time to meet sorceress with hesitation — one may be nervous

parts.note: a witch is a sorceress
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An encounter with a sorceress makes someone falter nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition also hints at the British sense of a keen birdwatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a jittery tic or jumpy manner is one who twitches, perhaps from nerves.

clue.text: Thrilling, being able to be switched on?

definitions.meaning: exciting, giving a jolt of excitement
powered by current, so operated by a switch

explanation.surface: Something exciting precisely because it can be turned on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes an exciting atmosphere and also appliances powered by current.

clue.text: Attlee was involved with reform (not half!), establishing this

definitions.text: Attlee was involved with reform (not half!), establishing this

indicators.note: being involved means the letters are tangled together and rearranged
only half of the word reform is kept, its first three letters

explanation.surface: Clement Attlee's post-war government brought in sweeping reform and set up a national system.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix ATTLEE WAS with REF, the first half of 'reform'. Clement Attlee was the UK Labour Prime Minister from 1945 whose government founded the National Health Service and social security system.
explanation.definitionFit: Attlee's government created the system of state benefits and healthcare, which is exactly what the clue describes him establishing.

clue.text: Greek character nicked sawn-off weapon

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: the word for nicked has its end sawn off, losing its last letter

parts.note: nicked means stole

explanation.surface: A Greek thief has stolen a shortened shotgun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sawn-off' looks like it describes the weapon, but it cuts the final E from STOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun is a type of weapon.

clue.text: Car leaving Nicaragua crushed lizard

indicators.note: crushing the letters breaks them up into a new order, once the car is gone

explanation.surface: A reptile run over by a car in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes C, A, R out of NICARAGUA, and 'crushed' rearranges the rest, NIAGUA.
explanation.definitionFit: This large tropical American reptile is a kind of lizard.

clue.text: Time to do something? Sensitivity needed

parts.note: to act is to do something

explanation.surface: It's time to take action, but carefully and delicately.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomacy and delicacy in dealing with others is a synonym for sensitivity.

clue.text: Getting rid of the female guarding one — worrying about that

indicators.note: the word for worrying goes around the other pieces

parts.note: caring about something can mean worrying over it

indicators.note: the female pronoun encloses the numeral, guarding it

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A protective woman fretting over a dismissal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting rid of' is a verb phrase, matching the -ing form of the answer: to cashier is to dismiss from service.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss them dishonourably, so the word means getting rid of someone.

clue.text: Instruments producing one sort of note, first to last

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is moved to the end

parts.note: a sharp is a note raised by a semitone

explanation.surface: Musical instruments that sound a particular kind of note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' moves the S of SHARP to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: These stringed instruments are plucked, an example of musical instruments.

clue.text: Priest very briefly appearing in garland

indicators.note: the short letter shows up inside the garland word

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
V is the short form of very

explanation.surface: A cleric makes a brief appearance wearing a garland.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Levi founded the tribe from whom the Levite priests descended, so his name stands for a priest.

clue.text: Growth of the furniture industry?

parts.note: growth here is what grows on an animal, and the stuffing once used in sofas and chairs

explanation.surface: A question about expansion in the business of making furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' suggests economic expansion; it means something grown, the coat of an animal used to stuff upholstery.
explanation.definitionFit: The mane and tail strands of a stallion were traditionally used as stuffing in upholstered chairs and sofas.

clue.text: Place on Italian coast with very big island to the west

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very big

indicators.note: in an across answer the island word runs leftwards, westwards, so its letters are read backwards

parts.note: an ait is a small river island

explanation.surface: Directions to a coastal town in Italy beside a large island further west.
explanation.walkthrough: AIT is a small island in a river, a word mostly heard of the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient port of Rome, lying at the mouth of the Tiber on the coast.

clue.text: Row when there's less than complete observation of instructions

indicators.note: only part of the word instructions is taken, the letters inside it

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out because someone failed to follow the rules fully.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop INS and S from 'instructions' to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy disturbance or quarrel is a synonym for a row.

clue.text: Daughter wearing a kilt's dancing somewhere in Scotland

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters wear the daughter's letter, holding it inside
the letters dance into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl in a kilt is performing a Highland dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns A KILTS into STKILA, and 'wearing' puts D inside before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: This remote archipelago lies far out in the Atlantic off the Outer Hebrides, a Scottish location.
